name: append-two-fields-shared-target
description: WRIT-201's reachable case: two different body fields, 'x' and 'y', are separately declared as append rules sharing one target ('log') under one exact (op_type, op_version) envelope — nothing in spec/fold.md §5 forbids this, the same way a version bump or a second op_type sharing a target is allowed, and CheckTargetCollision (spec/fieldrules.go) permits it because both rules agree on every merge attribute. A single operation writes both fields at once. Every matching rule MUST apply its write (spec/fold.md §5's 'every rule that matches an operation applies'), not only the first one a rule table happens to list: the folded list carries both entries, not one. Before WRIT-201, engine/internal/fold broke after the first matching rule per op and dropped the second field's entry, while spec/reffold.go already applied both. The list order is fixed by spec/fold.md §5's canonical rule order — a target's matching rules contribute in ascending (op_type, op_version, field), so 'x' precedes 'y' — and by nothing else. These two rules are deliberately labelled so that sorting the labels yields the reverse order (the 'y' rule first): an implementation that took its order from the sequence its rule table happens to list, load or enumerate rules in, rather than from the rules themselves, folds this vector to ['y-val', 'x-val'] and fails it.
